title: Can character sprite s not be pixels/ sprite s?

posts.author: Agate
posts.body:
I am confused and I can't seem to type the key words to find out for myself lol so thanks in advance
Anyway I noticed the enemies basically have a fullbody art for SV battles. SO can the heros also be fullbody art for the heros side? or Do they need to be sprites?
Like I've been messing around with the system settings and I found out I can use old PNG drawings I had and have them as enemies in battles. I can also crop the face to make conversations. Sure the resolution is smaller but it doesn't seem to make them pixelated or is it sprited lol
So I don't see a reason why the hero's SV are sprites.
Oh I guess same question for the walking sprites. I imagine those can look like chibi version of the heros or at least smoother looking then the pixel/sprite look

posts.author: ATT_Turan
posts.body:
You seem to have some terminology mixed up which isn't helpful for your searches or explanations
1 - "sprite" means any 2D image used in a video game. Everything you see in RPG Maker is a sprite.
2 - All images are made of pixels. None of the artwork you're talking about has been hand-drawn or 3D-modeled, so it's all pixel art.
So everything you're talking about with comparing to enemies and such are pixel sprites.
That being said, the answers to your questions are right in MV's documentation. Click Help -> Contents -> Documentation -> Asset Standards for a full description of the character sheet and SV battler sheet formats. They can be whatever sizes you want and you can put whatever kind of artwork you like in them.
As a side tip, you're likely to get more/better answers if you take a few moments to format your post. Clicking into a thread to see a big block of text is off-putting to many people

posts.author: gstv87
posts.body:
Agate said:
SO can the heros also be fullbody art for the heros side?
Click to expand...
yes-n't.
*since* the sprites are animated, requiring *multiple frames* to be rendered in sequence, requiring *them* to be passed *to* the engine as a single block, the larger the sprite, the larger the file.
multiply that by the amount of individual characters, you end up in the hundreds of megabytes for sprites alone.
if you don't care about size, yes, go right ahead... as long as it's formatted correctly, it'll render.
it's just not practical for portability or performance with what the engine is designed for.

posts.author: Andar
posts.body:
As explained above, sprites (both walking and battler) can be any size as long as the rules for them are followed. And as long as the screen is big enough to fit them while your computers RAM buffer has to be large enough to hold the entire picture.
I once wrote a tutorial on that to help people understand how to create larger sprites, because that requires mathematics. It might help you in lerning some terms as well:
How to create your own templates (any sprite or battler sheet)
Time and time again people who want to create their own sprites are asking for pre-made empty/framed templates because they can't work without them. And they don't even understand how limiting that is.  Templates are crutches - bad crutches to be precise, because if you need a premade template...
